values.Background: The Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) was a crude oil pipeline running from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia across Jordan, southern Syria (including the Golan Heights), and into Lebanon, terminating at the Sidon (Zahrani) Mediterranean export terminal. Constructed 1947-1950 by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company (a subsidiary of Aramco) using 30-inch and 31-inch steel pipe over a 1,213-1,214 km route, with six main pumping stations (Nariya, Qaisumah, Rafha, Badanah, Turaif in Saudi Arabia; Qaryatain in Jordan). Initial capacity 320,000 bpd, expanded via auxiliary pumping in 1957 to ~450,000 bpd and a peak nameplate of ~500,000 bpd. The cross-border line ceased operating in 1976 as the Lebanese Civil War began and supertankers eroded its economics; the Saudi and Jordanian portions continued intermittently until 1983/1990. Final 'de-cruding' (cleaning of residual crude) was completed in 2001. Designated Saudi Arabia's first industrial heritage site in December 2020.

values.Background: The Qatif-Qaisumah gathering line is the 507 km / 315 mi Saudi-internal segment of the Trans-Arabian Pipeline system. It gathered crude from the Qatif and Abqaiq field areas on the Persian Gulf coast of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and delivered it to Qaisumah, where the main 1,213 km Tapline mainline began its run northwest across Jordan, Syria, and Lebanon to the Sidon Mediterranean terminal. Built 1947-1950 alongside the mainline by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company (Aramco subsidiary). Operations wound down through the 1980s and ceased in 1990; final de-cruding 2001.

values.Background: C.A.T. Group (est. 1937) built this 42-inch, 220-km pipeline segment as an EPC-LSTK project to expand crude oil throughput capacity on the East-West Pipeline (Petroline) corridor. The project is named 'Expand Shaybah-Abqaiq Pipeline Capacity' by the contractor, reflecting Aramco's program-level objective of increasing total system capacity for Shaybah crude from field to export terminal. Scope included 2 launcher/receiver areas, 5 mainline valve stations, and 6 surge relief skids. C.A.T. has extensive history on the Petroline corridor, having previously completed a 536-km, 48-inch East-West crude oil pipeline segment.

values.Background: Stroytransgaz signed the EPC contract on March 31, 2007, for approximately $100 million. The 217-km, 30-inch pipeline connects GOSP-4 to the existing SHBAB-1 crude pipeline system within the Shaybah field area. Welding was completed by June 2008 at rates of up to 2 km/day, with four temporary worker villages built along the desert route. Full project completion was delayed from June 2008 to late 2009/early 2010. The pipeline supported Phase 1 expansion of Shaybah from 500,000 to 750,000 bpd of Arabian Extra Light crude.
